findings.title: Embedded-post author link swaps light and dark colours
findings.body: This was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The correct dark-theme conversion preserves that as the light branch and uses scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) for dark, but the change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)) — both branches are swapped. Light themes therefore get a much lighter author-link colour than before and dark themes get a much darker one, the opposite of the intended contrast.

findings.title: Custom-message-length swaps light and dark colours
findings.body: This was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The change writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)), swapping the two values. Light themes lose the original 70% colour (regressing existing appearance) and dark themes receive 70% instead of the complementary 30%, so the branches should be choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)).

findings.title: Topic-map h3 changes the existing light-theme colour
findings.body: This was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), and the corresponding desktop rule was correctly converted to choose(..., 20%, ..., 80%). Here it is converted to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)), so the unchanged light theme gets 50% instead of 20% and the dark theme gets 50% instead of 80%. Mobile topic-map headings become noticeably lighter/less contrasted than intended and inconsistent with desktop.

findings.title: Group-member name changes the existing light-theme colour
findings.body: This .group-member-info .name rule was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). It is converted to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% for dark. Both themes therefore render a mid-grey different from the intended 30%/70% pair, lightening the name on the default light theme.

findings.title: Missed scale-color($primary) conversion for category badge-notification
findings.body: This PR's stated purpose is to make every scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...) usable on dark themes via dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, ...)), and it converts the identical 50% rules throughout this file. Line 115, .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification, still uses bare color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%). On a dark theme $primary is light, so scaling its lightness to 50% yields a dark colour on a dark background, leaving this badge count poorly contrasted while neighbouring elements adapt.
